current_example.title: Example: Finding the Surface Area of a Cylinder

q-117991.name: Question 1
q-117991.problem: The radius of the base of a cylinder is $3\,\text{ft}$ and its height is $4\,\text{ft}.$ Find the lateral surface area of the cylinder.
q-117991.worked_solution:
We can calculate the lateral surface area of a cylinder using the formula

$$
{S}_{L}=2\pi rh,
$$

where $r$ is the radius and $h$ is the height of the cylinder.

Substituting $r=3\,\text{ft}$ and $h=4\,\text{ft}$ into the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}_{L} & =2\pi (3)(4)=24\pi \,{\text{ft}}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-117991.html:
Question 1
?

The radius of the base of a cylinder is 3ft and its height is 4ft. Find the lateral surface area of the cylinder.

a
72πft2
b
12πft2
c
24πft2
d
48πft2
e
36πft2
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We can calculate the lateral surface area of a cylinder using the formula

SL=2πrh,

where r is the radius and h is the height of the cylinder.

Substituting r=3ft and h=4ft into the formula, we get

SL=2π(3)(4)=24πft2.

q-107673.html:
Question 4
?

Determine the lateral surface area of the cylinder above.

a
336πin2
b
256πin2
c
168in2
d
48in2
e
126πin2
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We can calculate the lateral surface area of a cylinder using the formula

SL=2πrh,

where r is the radius and h is the height of the cylinder.

Substituting r=12in and h=14in into the formula, we get

SL=2π(12)(14)=336πin2.
